annotations.text:
Two homes for someone who is not building the app.

Not a mode: a different person. Which home you get is decided once, at setup, and the rail follows from it — a clean page with a twelve-item rail beside it is not a clean page.

Home answers "what should I look at". Today answers "what am I doing now, and next". The developer dashboard is untouched.

Light by default here, because that is what this person's machine looks like; there is a dark switch above each artboard.

The managers are the page.

Three tiles, one line of goal each, and one state word — and the words are the point: "one item is stuck", not "1 blocked". Same count, different reader.

One thing may want you at a time. If two managers are stuck it says one sentence and the second waits; everything queued is in Team, one tap away. A clean page that grows a list is a dashboard with more white space.

Today is the calendar's own day, not a second one — otherwise two day views drift the first week.

The dashed row in the gap is the whole idea: the largest free stretch after now, the smallest habit that fits and is behind, one button. It is drawn here and does not exist yet; habits are step 3 on the calendar board.

The habit ticks carry the same warning at the bottom of their card rather than pretending.

Read this before agreeing to the pictures.

Almost everything on both pages already exists — the managers, what needs you, today, due, focus. That is the only reason a third home is affordable.

Four things are not built, and one of them is a promise rather than a panel: an Ask bar that cannot act is a chat window wearing a search box. Draw it last.
